name: Horn of Arra'chea
summary: Across Mulgore, young hunters track Arra'chea at Cairne Bloodhoof's call. The horn proves they can find prey and provide for the Shu'halo.

sections.title: A Chieftain's Test
sections.body: After the Rites of the Earthmother, a youth may take a place atop Thunder Bluff. Yet High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof still asks his people to prove their worth. For the tauren, hunting ties their identity to lasting harmony with the land. So Cairne sends young hunters after Arra'chea, a massive, solitary kodo bull that roams the grasslands below. Taking the bull's horn proves they can track prey across vast distances.

sections.title: Providing for the Tribe
sections.body: Arra'chea's horn helps sustain Thunder Bluff as well as display a hunter's strength. Tauren make use of every part of a slain beast. The trophy tells the High Chieftain where Arra'chea fell. Then gathering parties can descend into the plains and harvest the kodo's thick hide and rich meat for the fledgling capital.

faq.q: What is the Horn of Arra'chea?
faq.answer: Arra'chea's horn comes from the powerful, elusive kodo roaming Mulgore's plains. Hunters bring it to Cairne Bloodhoof as a rite of passage and proof of their tracking skill.
Arra'chea is a renowned kodo bull that circles the grasslands northeast of Thunder Bluff. His strength and wide migratory route make him difficult quarry for hunters proving their worth to the tribe.

faq.q: Why does Cairne Bloodhoof ask for this trophy?
faq.answer: Cairne Bloodhoof asks for the trophy because he expects his people to keep proving their worth. Tracking and killing Arra'chea shows a hunter's dedication to the traditions of the Earthmother and provides resources for the community.

faq.q: What happens to the rest of the beast after it is killed?
faq.answer: Tauren use every part of the hunted animal. After the horn confirms the kill, Cairne sends a gathering party into Mulgore to collect the hide and meat for Thunder Bluff.

angles.text: As a tauren, presenting Arra'chea's horn to High Chieftain Cairne marks a rite of passage. It proves you are ready to sustain and defend your people atop Thunder Bluff.
As a hunter, tracking Arra'chea's circular path across Mulgore tests the stalking and wilderness survival skills valued in your calling.
